records.answer:
A fully unsupervised run should verify its output against relevant tests or clear success criteria before calling the task done. Task completion should be gated on those checks passing, so trust is earned through verification rather than assumed. [Source 1]

To keep a long session from drifting, use plan mode for non-trivial or risky work so assumptions and direction can be corrected before coding; direct compaction to preserve important decisions and constraints; and use rewind to recover from a wrong turn without restarting from scratch. Also choose the right level of supervision: hands-on review for unfamiliar or high-stakes work, and autonomous, goal-based work for clearly scoped, lower-risk tasks. [Source 2]
